reviews.title: Great BBQ
reviews.snippet:
Been here several times. Keep coming back.

Great BBQ. Have several different options for protein and sides.

I like the sampler with brisket, sausage, and beef rib. Very tasty!

The only sides I have tried are cole slaw, green beans, and creamed corn. All excellent.

I have never had to wait for a table but I'm sure they do get busy at times. 

Very convenient if you are in downtown Austin at one of the conference hotels.
tips: Not sure if they have A/C but they do have air moving so we were comfortable.

reviews.title: Please go somewhere else.
reviews.snippet: I don’t really ever write bad reviews but I wasted $65 here for some of the worst tasting bbq I’ve ever had, and that wasn’t even with alcohol.  I wanted to get the sampler but they were out of brisket. The waitress at the register sad I could get it and substitute for chicken or turkey. I asked if I would get a discount since brisket is much more expensive. She said no. I couldn’t make sense of spending $40 for a sampler with no brisket. I ended up getting the pulled pork. It had no bbq or smoke flavor what so ever and tasted like it had been cooked in a crockpot with bbq sauce poured over it. It was watery as well which is what made me think it was not even smoked. I ate 3 bites and couldn’t make myself eat any more. I got potato salad and creamed corn for the sides. The waitress said these were best sellers. The potato salad was extremely bland. It had no taste of anything really.  There were some red peppers, maybe pimento, in it but no salt at all or pepper. The creamed corn was ok but it was just canned corn and heavy cream cooked until the cream thickened. The white bread slice was stale from sitting out in the air.  I was so excited to get to try Texas Bbq for the first time and this feels like a sad excuse for it. Please save your money and go anywhere else. I don’t mind paying a lot of money for good food, but I threw 2/3 of my plate in the garbage.  I’m about to eat a protein bar and nurse my much lighter wallet.
tips: Don’t waste your money here. The food just isn’t good and it’s so expensive to be so bad.

reviews.title: Not Any More!
reviews.snippet:
Sorry. 

Used to be a good spot but someone raised their prices without quality 

Sausage wrap is a 5 inch piece of sausage on a piece of white bread ? Paying for that at a food truck would be an insult let alone here. 

That was our last time coming here after decades of.

reviews.title: Great Barbecue in Austin
reviews.snippet: The brisket is so good. Eat inside. This is what a BBQ restaurant should look like.  Located near the lake downtown. I recommend the potato salad

reviews.title: Decent Old School style downtown BBQ
reviews.snippet:
I have to qualify that being from Memphis are standards are very high.
I really liked the feel of the place. It has a great old school BBQ feel. We ordered the combo w/ pulled pork, sausage & brisket. the wife had half rack of pork ribs. Sides of cream corn & BBQ beans. Brisket was the best item. it gets 4 out of 5 rating. Pulled pork not bad but middle of the road. 
Sausage nothing special. Pork Ribs dry style too crispy but still tender on the bone a 2. Cream Corn a 4 and BBQ Beans a 2.5. Sauce a 4. They had peach cobbler ala mode strong 4+. 
Easy walk reasonably priced not the worst by any stretch.

reviews.title: Convenient location for BBQ
reviews.snippet:
We were cramming in a day in Austin and did a great tour that left from the Austin 
Visitor Center and this place was nearby.

We stepped up and ordered at the counter. When in Texas - gotta be brisket and
it did not disappoint. The ribs were just ok and the sides were fine,

Not much of a vibe - think of it as a quick BBQ joint in a convenient location,
with decor that looks like worn- but the star of the show - The Brisket made it 
OK!!

reviews.title: Best Texas brisket but that's it.
reviews.snippet: You go here for the food which was delicious - we shared the sampler plate as we had eaten already - the  place itself is a little run down and the staff not the best, but who cares.
